title: Low-overhead request envelope and deterministic sampling integrator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: implement a lightweight request envelope header and deterministic sampling algorithm across Redwood SDKs and edge middleware to reduce tracing noise, keep tail latency stable, and provide reproducible sampled traces for postmortem analysis. This ticket covers design, SDK adapters (Node/Python/Go), middleware for internal gateways, and rollout plan for a safe canary.

Motivation: current tracing sampling is noisy and non-deterministic which makes it hard to reproduce incidents and correlating trace+logs for low-frequency errors. We need a single, compact request envelope header that carries minimal provenance (request_id, route_hash, sampled_hint) and a deterministic sampling policy that can be evaluated in constant time in the fast path.

High-level approach:
- Envelope header: introduce X-RI-Envelope (base64 URLsafe JSON <= 128 bytes) containing {rid, rhash, shint, ts}. SDKs provide builders/validators; gateways have fast C-like parser.
- Deterministic sampling: HMAC-SHA256(rid + secret_salt) mod 10000 < sampling_rate*100 => deterministic based on request_id + salt. Default sampling_rate 1%. Bucketed sampling allows targeted increases per-route via route_hash mapping.
- Fast-path design: parsing and sampling decision are implemented as non-allocating code in each SDK where possible; fallback to safe parser when header malformed. Goal overhead < 2 microseconds for Node and Go, < 4 microseconds for Python on warm VMs.
- Backwards compatibility: if header absent, fall back to probabilistic sampler (current behavior). Header is optional and marked opt-in per client release.

Acceptance criteria:
1) SDKs (Node, Python, Go) expose envelope builder and validator APIs and publish sampling decision as trace attribute (ri.sampling.decision).
2) Middleware for edge proxy and internal gateway can parse X-RI-Envelope and make routing/sampling decisions without heap allocations.
3) Deterministic sampler matches reference implementation and is configurable via runtime flags and per-route overrides in rollout config.
4) End-to-end tests (unit+integration) and benchmarking artifacts attached. Measured added p50 p99 latency impact <= 2us / 5us respectively on our perf harness.
5) Gradual rollout plan documented with canary metric thresholds and automatic rollback hooks in Console.

Non-goals: distributed sampling coordination, full trace rehydration, and changing existing trace IDs are out of scope for this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs provide X-RI-Envelope builder + validator and expose sampling decision attribute
Edge and gateway middleware parse header in fast-path with <2us overhead on Go/Node
Deterministic sampler conforms to reference test vectors included in repo
E2E test suite and benchmark results checked into observability/perf and linked
Runbook and Console canary thresholds documented and ready for rollout
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after architecture sync. Initial API sketched for Node/Python/Go.
2026-03-11: PoC deterministic sampler implemented in Go (internal repo). Local microbench: decision cost ~0.7us alloc-free.
2026-03-12: Node SDK patch added fast-path parser using Buffer.readUInt32 + memchr; measured overhead ~1.3us on warm lambda. Raised a follow-up for macOS build flags.
2026-03-13: Design review with PM and Security. Security requested explicit opt-in, proof-of-privacy for route_hash and salt handling. Updated design to HMAC with key rotation window.

2026-03-14: PR opened for Python SDK with C-extension optional fast-path (fallback pure Python). Benchmarks show 3.8us on warm CPython with C-extension, 9.1us pure Python. Marked C-extension as experimental for now.
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-10): Initial scope. Need to confirm header size limit with infra (edge header max=8192). Proposing 128 byte max to keep envelope cheap and fit in common proxies.
Jonas Reed (2026-03-11): PoC results attached in PR. Suggest we expose 'ri.sample.override' attribute in SDKs so support engineers can force-sample in Console for investigations.

Priya Kapoor - Security (2026-03-13): Approved concept but requires key rotation plan for HMAC salt and minimization of PII. Ensure route_hash is non-reversible; add docs describing privacy guarantees.
Ethan Park - Performance (2026-03-12): Noted Python C-extension increases build complexity. Recommend shipping Node/Go fast-paths first and Python fallback for canary.
Design review notes (2026-03-13): Keep envelope JSON schema stable; add version byte to header so future changes are forward-compatible. Use urlsafe base64 without padding to save bytes.
QA (2026-03-14): Added integration tests for malformed envelopes (should not crash) and for sampling boundary cases (rate 0%, 100%, and 1% with exact RID values).
